claim: RAT-SQL does name-based schema linking by string-matching question n-grams (length 1-5) against column/table names as exact/partial(subsequence)/no match, encoding these as directional relation labels that bias a relation-aware self-attention encoder.
quote: for all n-grams of length 1 to 5 in the question, we determine (1) whether it exactly matches the name of a column/table (exact match); or (2) whether the n-gram is a subsequence of the name ... M is one of ExactMatch, PartialMatch, or NoMatch.

claim: Schema linking aligns NL questions with schema elements; using the full schema adds irrelevant context, token overhead and hallucinations that cut accuracy, and prior methods show a recall/false-positive tradeoff (CHESS 97.12% recall / 30.57% FPR; RSL-SQL 93.28% recall / 68.23% FPR), which a bidirectional table-first + column-first union approach tries to balance.
quote: Schema linking---the process of aligning natural language questions with database schema elements ... Using the full schema introduces irrelevant context, increases token overhead, and often leads to hallucinations ... CHESS achieves the highest recall (97.12%) but at the cost of an elevated false positive rate (30.57%) ... RSL-SQL reports strong recall (93.28%) yet suffers from a high FPR (68.23%)

claim: CRUSH4SQL instructs an LLM to hallucinate a minimal schema for a query, then uses collective dense retrieval against the real schema, achieving higher recall than prior retrieval methods on large databases (up to 17,844 schema elements).
quote: instruct[s] an LLM to hallucinate a minimal DB schema deemed adequate to answer the query ... leads to significantly higher recall than SOTA retrieval-based augmentation methods

claim: A 2024 survey groups schema linking into three eras (string-matching/similarity, neural-network alignment, LLM in-context-learning), notes it identifies the relevant tables/columns and is essential for accuracy, and is even more critical in the LLM era due to input-length limits.
quote: Early research primarily focused on string matching techniques ... researchers have employed deep neural networks ... leverage their strong reasoning capabilities for schema linking ... This step is essential for improving the performance of the Text-to-SQL task ... In the LLM era, schema linking has become even more critical due to the input length limitations of LLMs.

claim: CHESS retrieves schema-relevant values via model-generated keywords, locality-sensitive hashing for ANN value search and a vector DB for semantic catalog search, then applies adaptive schema pruning (column filter, table select, final column select); ablation shows giving the LLM all information confuses it, so selective retrieval is crucial.
quote: LSH is an effective technique for approximate nearest-neighbor searches ... preprocesses database catalogs into a vector database ... providing an LLM with all available information can confuse the model and selective retrieval is crucial for achieving higher performance.
